memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason: follow‑up of migraine and asthma.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports throbbing bilateral headaches twice weekly, mild exertional wheezing relieved by salbutamol inhaler.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/82 mmHg, weight 78 kg, height 1.68 m, BMI 27.6 (obese). Respiratory exam shows mild bilateral expiratory wheeze; cardiovascular normal; neurological exam normal.
IMPRESSION: 1) Migraine – continue propranolol 40 mg OD for prophylaxis. 2) Asthma – currently controlled on budesonide‑formoterol 200/6 inhaler BD and salbutamol SOS. Order fasting lipid profile and fasting blood sugar (annual screen). Order neurological examination and CT head to exclude secondary headache causes. Order spirometry with reversibility.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue all medications. Schedule investigations today. Return if: new severe headache, visual loss, weakness, speech difficulty, fever >39°C, worsening wheeze, breathlessness at rest, or blood in sputum. Ask patient to repeat the list. Advice: reduce refined carbohydrates, increase daily walk to 30 min, avoid fried foods.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason: review of headache frequency and lipid results.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Headaches reduced to once weekly; mild fatigue noted. No asthma exacerbations in past month.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/84 mmHg, weight 77 kg, BMI 27.3 (obese). Respiratory clear. No neurological deficits.
IMPRESSION: Migraine – prophylaxis partially effective; consider adding topiramate. Asthma – well controlled. Lipids show borderline high LDL; FBS elevated suggesting pre‑diabetes. Continue statin‑lifestyle advice.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase topiramate to 25 mg HS (already) and add propranolol 40 mg OD unchanged. Initiate metformin 500 mg BD for pre‑diabetes. Advise low‑glycemic diet, repeat lipids and FBS in 3 months. Return if: headache >3 days continuous, visual aura, chest pain, dyspnea on exertion, fever >39°C, or hypoglycaemic symptoms. Advice: increase vegetable intake, limit sweets, walk 4 km weekly.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Spirometry with reversibility: FEV1 2.1 L (78% predicted), FVC 2.8 L (85% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.75. Post‑bronchodilator FEV1 2.4 L (88% predicted), improvement 14% – positive reversibility consistent with asthma.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I have been using my salbutamol inhaler only twice a week and my Asthma Control Test score is 22 (well controlled). Headaches are less troubling but I still feel occasional neck tension.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason: autumn review; assess flu vaccine need and metabolic parameters.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: No headache attacks in past 4 weeks; occasional mild nasal congestion. No wheeze.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/80 mmHg, weight 76 kg, BMI 26.9 (overweight). Respiratory clear. No focal neurology.
IMPRESSION: Migraine – well controlled on current regimen. Asthma – controlled. Lipids: repeat shows LDL 3.0 mmol/L, HDL 1.2 mmol/L, triglycerides 1.5 mmol/L. FBS 5.8 mmol/L (improved). Patient eligible for annual influenza vaccine due to chronic lung disease.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue all meds. Give inactivated influenza vaccine today (0.5 mL IM). Advise maintain weight <23 kg/m2 via diet and brisk walking 30 min daily. Return if: sudden severe headache, fever >39°C, productive cough with coloured sputum, chest pain, or shortness of breath at rest. Ask patient to repeat list.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason: post‑vaccination follow‑up and metabolic review.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports no flu‑like symptoms after vaccine; occasional mild headache after long work days.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/82 mmHg, weight 75 kg, BMI 26.5 (overweight). Respiratory clear.
IMPRESSION: Migraine – stable; occasional tension‑type headache likely stress‑related. Asthma – well controlled. Metformin tolerated; FBS 5.5 mmol/L, LDL 2.8 mmol/L, HDL 1.3 mmol/L, triglycerides 1.4 mmol/L – improving toward targets.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds. Encourage stress‑management techniques, maintain aerobic activity 150 min/week. Return if: new neurological deficit, fever >39°C, worsening wheeze, unexplained weight loss, or gastrointestinal bleeding. Advice: reduce saturated fat, increase whole grains.
